chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Mad'ini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
He disliked wearing a shirt bordered with silk, and disliked wearing silk, and wearing embroidered clothing, and disliked the red turban, for it is the turban of Iblis.
ai.seo_question: What clothing items did Imam al-Sadiq dislike and why?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates specific garments associated with luxury and distinctiveness, including silk-bordered shirts, pure silk, and embroidered clothing, while singling out the red turban (*mitharah*) as the 'turban of Iblis.' This reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of linking sartorial choices to spiritual humility and distinguishing between permissible adornment and ostentatious display that may lead to arrogance. The prohibition of the red turban specifically connects to historical practices of the elite and the symbolic association of red with pride or satanic influence in Islamic tradition.
